title: Well-Architected Framework and cloud design principles

kcs.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is a set of best practices and review questions for evaluating a cloud architecture across six pillars; it guides design reviews and does not deploy or change resources.

Core AWS design principles include designing for failure by removing every single point of failure, decoupling components so one failing part does not break the rest, and using elasticity instead of fixed capacity.
AWS design principles treat servers as disposable resources and favour automation: replace a faulty server with a fresh one built automatically instead of repairing it by hand.

problem_ideas: A team patches a broken web server for 3 hours each incident: which design principle would they follow instead?
An order service calls the payment service directly and both crash together: name the principle that fixes this.
Decide whether the Well-Architected Framework or the Cloud Adoption Framework fits 'review our workload for risks'.
Find the single point of failure in a three-tier design and name the principle it breaks.
Spot the false claim: 'The Well-Architected Framework automatically fixes misconfigured resources.'
Match four design principles to short scenarios (decouple, design for failure, disposable servers, automate).
